skills.name: Enterprise Sales
skills.honest_assessment: This is genuinely my strongest skill. I can navigate complex organizations, build executive relationships, and close deals. This isn't just resume talk—I have the numbers to back it up.

skills.name: Communication & Storytelling
evidence: Can explain complex technical concepts to non-technical audiences
skills.honest_assessment: Teaching + sales = I can explain anything to anyone. This is what I do best, and it's the foundation of everything else I do well.

skills.name: Stakeholder Management
evidence: Built executive relationships at VP+ level
Navigated Salesforce acquisition with 0 customer churn
skills.honest_assessment: I can map organizational dynamics, identify hidden blockers, and build consensus. This is really just applied psychology with business stakes.

skills.name: Relationship Building
evidence: Built internal champion networks at every company
skills.honest_assessment: I build genuine relationships, not transactional ones. People take my calls because they trust me, not because I'm persistent.

skills.name: Product Thinking

Identified features that became product updates
skills.honest_assessment: Good instincts from years of customer-facing work. I understand user problems deeply. Still learning to validate assumptions properly and prioritize ruthlessly.

skills.name: Python
evidence: Working with APIs, file processing, basic web servers
skills.honest_assessment: Functional and improving daily. I can build working tools that solve real problems. Not writing production-grade code for Fortune 500s, but I ship things that work.

skills.name: JavaScript / Web Dev
evidence: Working with APIs and frontend frameworks
skills.honest_assessment: Can build functional web apps. Frontend design is not my strength—I focus on functionality over aesthetics. Still learning modern frameworks.

skills.name: AI API Integration
evidence: Working with Gemini and OpenAI APIs daily
skills.honest_assessment: I know how to use LLM APIs effectively—prompt engineering, streaming, context management. I'm not building models, but I can build with them.

skills.name: Data Visualization
evidence: Years of helping customers build dashboards
skills.honest_assessment: I know what good looks like and can build basic visualizations. Not a designer, but I understand the principles of presenting data clearly.

skills.name: System Architecture
skills.honest_assessment: I know enough to build things that work. Scaling and optimization are areas where I need mentorship. I can architect small systems; large systems are aspirational.

skills.name: DevOps / Infrastructure
evidence: Deploy my own projects to Vercel
skills.honest_assessment: I can deploy to Vercel and set up basic CI. Kubernetes? AWS at scale? Docker orchestration? Not yet. Learning as I need it.

skills.name: Machine Learning Theory
evidence: Using ML/AI as a tool effectively
skills.honest_assessment: I use ML/AI as a tool, not as a practitioner. I can't build models from scratch, but I can build effective applications with them. The theory is something I'm actively studying.

skills.name: Databases
skills.honest_assessment: Can work with SQLite and write basic queries. Not designing schemas for high-scale systems. This is a clear growth area.

skills.name: Testing & QA
evidence: Writing basic tests for my projects
skills.honest_assessment: Honestly, this is a weakness. I ship fast and sometimes skip proper testing. Working on building better habits, but I'll be honest—it's not muscle memory yet.
